rows.name: MIXTRAL_PATH
rows.read_by: `t_tokenizers`, `t_llguidance`, `t_rinzler_tokens`, Rust unit tests of the `hf_tokenizers_ffi` crate (`t/t_tokenizers.cpp`, `t/t_llguidance.cpp`, `rust/tokenizers/src/lib.rs` and 1 more file)
rows.values: Path of a directory with the Mixtral model files. The C++ tests accept only an existing directory. The Rust tests open `tokenizer.json` in it.
rows.default: Unset: the C++ tests use `/opt/positron/weights/huggingface/mistralai/Mixtral-8x7B-Instruct-v0.1` or skip when it is missing. The Rust tests return and pass. Empty: the Rust tests open `/tokenizer.json`.
rows.effect: Gives the Mixtral tokenizer tests the directory of the model files. It enables 3 Rust unit tests. It replaces the fixed path in 3 C++ test programs.
rows.notes: The C++ tests ignore a value that is not an existing directory. They treat an empty value as unset. Rust: when `tokenizer.json` cannot be loaded, 2 tests fail and 1 test prints a skip message.

rows.name: PAUSE_HINT
rows.values: `0` or `1`, parsed with `std::stoi`. The test output labels `1` as `C0.1` and `0` as `C0.2`. Text that is not a number makes `std::stoi` throw.
rows.default: Unset: `1`.
rows.effect: Sets the hint argument of the CPU instruction `tpause` in the spin-wait benchmark. The main thread and the worker thread both use it.
rows.notes: Read only when `PAUSE_TYPE` is `tpause`. The test requires a value of at most `1`. The value is stored in 8 bits before that check. So `256` becomes `0` and passes.

evidence.quote: static uint8_t tpause_hint = 1;              // override by env-var when using 'tpause'

rows.name: PAUSE_LEN_NS
rows.values: Integer number of nanoseconds, parsed with `std::stoi`. Text that is not a number makes `std::stoi` throw.
rows.default: Unset: 500 nanoseconds.
rows.effect: Sets the `tpause` wait length of the main thread in the spin-wait benchmark. The worker thread always uses 500 nanoseconds.
rows.notes: Read only when `PAUSE_TYPE` is `tpause`. The value is stored as an unsigned 64-bit number. A negative number becomes a very large wait. The check `tpause_ns >= 0` cannot fail.

evidence.quote: static uint64_t tpause_ns = TPAUSE_WAIT_NS;  // override by env-var when using 'tpause'

rows.name: PAUSE_TYPE
rows.values: `tpause` selects the CPU instruction `tpause`. `none` selects a loop with no pause instruction. Any other text keeps the default. The match is exact.
rows.default: Unset: the CPU instruction `pause`.
rows.effect: Chooses the wait instruction of the spin-wait benchmark (a loop that polls a flag and does not sleep). The test case is `spin-wait loop with Intel pause/tpause`.
rows.notes: The test case skips on a CPU whose vendor is not Intel. `PAUSE_HINT` and `PAUSE_LEN_NS` are read only with `tpause`.

rows.name: PERFETTO_CAPTURE_REQUIRE_INTEGRATION
rows.values: Exactly `1` turns the requirement on. Any other text leaves it off.
rows.default: Unset: when `PERFETTO_BIN_DIR` has no executable `traced` and `perfetto`, the script prints `SKIP integration` and exits with status 0.
rows.effect: With `1`, the script fails with the message `integration required` when the Perfetto programs `traced` and `perfetto` are missing. It does not skip the integration checks.
rows.notes: CI sets `1` for the step `CI helper script tests` in `cmake-single-platform.yml` and `gcp-nix.yml`. The variable changes nothing when `PERFETTO_BIN_DIR` holds both programs.

evidence.quote: printf 'SKIP integration: set PERFETTO_BIN_DIR to a dir with traced+perfetto '

rows.name: PERFETTO_TEST_BIN_DIR
rows.values: Path of a directory that holds the Perfetto programs `traced` and `perfetto`.
rows.default: Unset: the test `test_launchers_do_not_start_targets_before_perfetto_is_ready` stops with `KeyError`.
rows.effect: The test `test_launchers_do_not_start_targets_before_perfetto_is_ready` starts the real `traced` and `perfetto` from this directory.
rows.notes: `flake.nix` sets it for the Nix check `perfetto-config`. That check runs `perfetto/test_perfetto.py`.

rows.name: RINZLER_PROXY_BIN
rows.values: Path of the `rinzler_proxy` program. `t/proxy/run_suite.sh` resolves a relative path against the checkout root. `t/proxy/rzproxy/launch.py` uses the text as it is.
rows.default: Unset: `gen/rinzler_proxy` in the checkout. Empty: `t/proxy/run_suite.sh` treats it as unset. `t/proxy/rzproxy/launch.py` does not apply the default.
rows.effect: Selects the `rinzler_proxy` program that the proxy test suites start. Except in the mode `test_rzproxy.py lib`, `t/proxy/run_suite.sh` exits with status 1 when the file is not executable.
rows.notes: CTest (the CMake test runner) sets it for `t_proxy_lib`, `t_proxy_llama31` and `t_proxy_gptoss` to the `rinzler_proxy` of the same build tree. The launcher raises `LaunchError` when the file is missing.

new_terms.definition: A test loop in `t/t_mwaitx.cpp` in which 2 threads pass a flag back and forth. Each thread polls the flag and does not sleep. The test records how many CPU cycles each wait takes.
The CMake test runner. `t/CMakeLists.txt` registers the tests that it runs.
A fake command that a test writes and puts first on `PATH`, so that the script under test runs it in place of the real command.

notes: 24 rows, none dropped. 9 rows are hand_set true, 15 rows are fixtures. MIXTRAL_PATH and RINZLER_PROXY_BIN behave differently per reader, and the rows say so. REAL_CHMOD has 3 setter files. set_in names 1 file and the notes cell names the other 2 files. RINZLER_MODEL_ROOT stays as a fixture row. No TRON program reads it. doc/distributed-dice-agent-guide.md uses it in an example command and does not explain it. Group choices: both Perfetto test variables are in tool-tests. The PAUSE_* variables and POS_VERBOSE_TEST are in hardware. RZ_TABLE_REPEAT is in other. The evidence quote for the yq query line of bin/ci/test/test-positron-dice-resource-map.sh stops before the pipe character of that line. This keeps the pipe character out of the file. Evidence quotes have the leading indentation of the source line removed.
